properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-31, arriving out of the alternate-design discussion. Nothing chosen.

HIS WORDS: "does each node in the graph have an associated git repo/branch field... when the agent wants to determine where something is, it can just look at the node. And in the case of an alternate design, maybe the nodes/edges of the alternate design project have git_repo/alternate_design_branch. Additionally, when something is in work, maybe it has the branch that it is being worked in... when it is merged to main, then the node is also updated to git_repo/main now. If we were really fancy, could maybe include the commit hash... Then there is explicit traceability with every node in the design with its git repo/branch/commit?"

═══ WHAT EXISTS TODAY, CHECKED ═══
NO node type carries a git coordinate. The nearest three, and none is this:
· `Artifact.location` + `checksum` — a path and a content hash. WHERE a file is, not which branch a NODE belongs to.
· `Resource.version` — "for a design-dependency: the version this design MEANS to depend on — a tag, a commit, a release". About depending on ANOTHER design.
· The export `stamp` — carries `reflow2_version` and the schema shape, and NO git coordinate at all.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR IT IS A TRAP THAT HAS ALREADY BITTEN ═══
The design graph does NOT branch with git: one store per DIRECTORY, shared by every branch checked out in it. A session on a feature branch writes into the same graph as main, and a plain export then carries the other branch's writes. That was caught once as FOUR PHANTOM DRIFTS and it would have merged cleanly — a silent wrong merge, which is the worst class this project recognises. A branch coordinate is exactly what would make that detectable rather than discovered.

═══ 🛑 AND THERE IS A CIRCULARITY THAT BOUNDS THE COMMIT HALF ═══
The design is exported to a FILE THAT LIVES IN THE REPO. A node therefore CANNOT carry the hash of the commit that contains it: writing the hash changes the file, which changes the commit. The commit field can only ever mean "the commit this was DERIVED FROM" or "last synced at" — never "the commit I am in". That is not fatal, and it is not what the idea assumes, so it has to be stated before anyone builds it.

═══ 🛑 AND THE CORE CANNOT COMPUTE IT ═══
`reflow2-core` does NO file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly — `reconcile_artifacts` makes the CALLER supply hashes for exactly this reason. So a git coordinate would be CALLER-SUPPLIED: a claim, not a computation. That is the shape that goes stale, and this session has recorded EIGHT instances today of a declared property nothing reads or populates.

⭐ THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WORK: `Artifact.checksum` is the same shape — a git-adjacent fact stored on a node — and it earns its keep ONLY because `reconcile_artifacts` recomputes it from disk and reports divergence. A branch field with no equivalent recomputation is decoration that will be wrong the first time somebody merges without updating it, which his own sentence anticipates ("then the node is ALSO UPDATED") and which nothing would notice.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
① PER-NODE repo/branch/commit, as proposed. Maximum traceability. ⚠️ 3,536 nodes each carrying a hand-maintained fact with no recomputation; goes stale on every merge; and the commit half cannot mean what it appears to.
② ON THE EXPORT STAMP ONLY — branch and commit recorded once per export, at the MCP layer where file I/O is already allowed. ⭐ CHEAPEST, and it catches the phantom-drift trap exactly, because that trap is a property of the EXPORT rather than of any node. ⚠️ Says nothing about an individual node's provenance, which is what he asked for.
③ ON THE ChangeEvent — the branch a change was made on, recorded at the moment of the write. ⭐ A ChangeEvent is already the "what moved and when" record, it is written once and never edited, so it CANNOT go stale the way a per-node field would. ⚠️ Answers "where was this changed" rather than "where does this live now".
④ ONLY ON ARTIFACTS, extending `location` with a repo/branch. ⭐ Artifacts are the nodes that actually correspond to files, and the recomputation machinery already exists there. ⚠️ Leaves every non-Artifact node — which is most of the graph — unlocated.
⑤ NOTHING, AND FIX THE TRAP DIRECTLY: have the export or `sync_status` warn when the working tree's branch differs from the one the last export was taken on. ⚠️ Solves the measured incident and none of the traceability he is asking for.

═══ ⚠️ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS ═══
(1) `dec:merge-three-way` settled that GIT IS THE DAG and reflow2 owns no branch machinery. Recording a coordinate is not owning the DAG, but ① edges toward reflow2 maintaining a parallel model of git state, which is the thing that decision refused.
(2) The idea's own update rule — "when merged to main, the node is also updated" — is a hand-maintained invariant with nothing checking it, which is the exact cause shape this project keeps finding: "a rule maintained by hand with nothing checking it is a rule that silently stops being true".
(3) It is not clear anybody has needed per-node location. The phantom-drift incident needed EXPORT-level branch awareness; the fork case needs to know which STORE a node is in, which the store path already answers.
properties.name: DECIDED 2026-09-16 — the git coordinate lives on the EXPORT, not on nodes: every export written inside a repository carries `taken_at` (branch, commit, dirty), kept while the content is unchanged; the coherence gate refuses an export about to be committed on a branch it was not taken on (options ② and ⑤ together); no per-node field
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm discipline — ideas as ideas, nothing promoted, counter-arguments beside rather than against.

The circularity and the no-file-IO constraint are recorded first because both bound what the idea can mean, and neither is visible from the proposal as stated: a node cannot carry its own commit, and the core cannot compute any git fact, so every option below is a caller-supplied claim rather than a derived one.
